name: Academic Advising
description: Our Academic Advisors are available to assist you with goal setting, career exploration, choosing a focus area, creating an education plan, selecting classes, reviewing semester maps, and applying for graduation.

name: Transfer Centers
description: Our Transfer Centers can help you transition to a four-year college including researching where you want to attend, learning about transferable courses, and applying for transfer scholarships.

name: Career Centers
description: Our Career Centers can help you decide on a career and choose the best academic program to get you there. You can also learn how to complete a job application, create a resume and interview effectively to help you land a job or internship.

name: Tutoring Centers
description: Our Tutoring Centers offer free tutoring and academic support services to assist students in achieving personal and academic success. One-on-one and group tutoring sessions are available.

name: Testing Resource Centers
description: The Testing Resources Centers provide a variety of testing services to assist students as they pursue their academic goals. COMPASS testing and other placement exams can be taken there.

name: College Libraries
description: CCC’s College Libraries offer electronic, database, and print media to support the scholarly work of students, faculty, and staff as well as individual and group library and information literacy instruction.

name: Financial Aid Offices
description: Our Financial Aid Offices work closely with students and families to provide financial assistance in the form of grants, loans and work-study from federal and state resources. For help filling out the FAFSA form, visit your college’s Financial Aid Office.

name: Scholarship opportunities (Financial Aid Offices)
description: Our Financial Aid Offices work closely with students and families to provide financial assistance in the form of grants, loans and work-study from federal and state resources. To learn about scholarships, visit your college’s Financial Aid Office.

name: Disability Access Centers
description: Our Disability Access Centers provide coordination and supportive services for students with documented disabilities. CCC makes every effort to integrate students with disabilities into all courses and programs.

name: Wellness Centers
description: Our Wellness Centers offer personal and group counseling, stress and time management coaching, and referrals to community resources including low-cost medical/dental care, emergency housing, groceries, legal services and child care.

name: Loaner laptop program
description: City Colleges of Chicago credit students may borrow a Windows laptop free of charge for up to 4 weeks. Laptops are issued on a first-come, first served basis.

name: Chicago Star Scholarship
description: City Colleges will provide waivers for all eligible tuition, books, and class materials not covered by financial aid.

name: Federal Pell Grant
description: A Federal Pell Grant provides grant funds to undergraduate students from low-income households. Unlike student loans, Pell Grants usually don’t need to be repaid.

name: Federal Work-Study
description: Federal Work-Study provides part-time jobs to students with financial need. Students can gain valuable work experience while earning money to help pay for college, career school, or trade school expenses.

name: Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)
description: Completing and submitting the FAFSA form is free—and it’s for more than just federal student aid. States, schools, and some private aid providers also use your FAFSA information to determine your eligibility for their financial aid programs.

name: Monetary Award Program (MAP)
description: MAP grants, which do not need to be repaid, are available to eligible Illinois residents who attend approved Illinois colleges and demonstrate financial need, based on the information provided on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA®). MAP grants can be applied only toward tuition and mandatory fees.

name: Alternative Application for Illinois Financial Aid
description: The Retention of Illinois Students & Equity (RISE) Act allows certain students who are not eligible for federal student aid, including undocumented students, to apply for state financial aid.

name: Priority Access for Returning MAP Recipients
description: Returning Monetary Award Program (MAP) recipients who file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA®) or Alternative Application for Illinois Financial Aid (Alternative Application) on or before a date established each year will receive priority access to annually appropriated MAP funds.

name: Undocumented Student Services
description: Each City College has a liaison for undocumented students and allies, who can help you navigate college offices and programs and who will listen to things you do not feel comfortable sharing with just anyone. An undocumented status does not affect admission, and no one will ask your status as part of enrollment. It may affect financial aid, scholarships, and grants.
contact_office: Undocumented Student Services Liaison (at your college)

name: Resources for Non-Eligible, Non-U.S. Citizens
description: ISAC's page lists information and assistance for non-U.S. citizens planning to attend college, including legal and other support services: FAQs on DACA from Homeland Security, a college advising guide for undocumented students, and the Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (an attorney referral list and student guides).

name: Food pantries at every college
description: There is a food pantry at every City College, and students are encouraged to use them as needed. Contact your college's Wellness Center for questions, hours, locations, and additional resources. Free grab-and-go snacks are also available at every college (City Colleges guide dated November 18, 2025).

name: Food Security for Life Initiative
description: City Colleges expanded its partnership with the Greater Chicago Food Depository. As of November 18, 2025: free grab-and-go snacks at every college; ready-to-take-home meals at Malcolm X, Kennedy-King, and Olive-Harvey Colleges (planned for all seven); and an expanded market planned to open at Kennedy-King in January 2026, with markets planned for all seven colleges. Check with your Wellness Center for what is available now.

name: Help with SNAP work requirements
description: Beginning December 1, 2025, many adults ages 18-64 without dependents under 14 face new federal work or volunteer requirements to keep receiving SNAP, with monthly reporting of hours. Some adults qualify for exemptions: manage your case in the ABE Manage My Case portal or call the Illinois Department of Human Services. City Colleges AmeriCorps VISTA members can connect you to volunteer opportunities that meet the requirements.
contact_office: Illinois Department of Human Services (IDHS); AmeriCorps VISTA members at City Colleges

name: Child care referrals (Wellness Centers)
description: Wellness Centers offer referrals to community resources including child care, along with low-cost medical/dental care, emergency housing, groceries, and legal services.

name: Free ESL classes (Adult Education)
description: City Colleges offers free ESL classes to learn or improve English for any reason. Register at ccc.edu/ae, where there are resources in Spanish, Polish, Arabic, and Simplified Chinese.

name: Free high school diploma preparation (Adult Education)
description: You can prepare for free at City Colleges to earn your high school diploma. Classes are offered in English and Spanish. Register at ccc.edu/ae.

name: Early College Program
description: Motivated juniors and seniors at Chicago high schools, regardless of citizenship status, can earn college credit for free through the City Colleges Early College Program.

name: Micro-internships
description: Micro-internships are short-term, paid professional assignments posted by employers across industries, ranging from about 10 to 40 hours of work. They let you build your resume.

name: Credit for Prior Learning (CPL)
description: Credit for Prior Learning, also known as Prior Learning Assessment, recognizes learning you have done outside the classroom, including work experience, employer training, military experience, independent study or research, professional certifications, civic activities, and volunteer service.

name: Reverse transfer
description: Reverse transfer lets you earn your City Colleges associate degree even after you transfer to a four-year institution.
